items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Now, Marlowe Morris is sitting between them.

ctx.x: So one night, Zoot's family came to hear him play. Zoot got lost. He didn't get on the bandstand all night long. He was bashful, shy. So anyway, one day Zoots driving us home. He says, "Man, I'm tired of driving." He said, "Can somebody drive?" I'm in the rumble seat. I say, "Yeah, I can drive." He says, "Come on and drive." I say, "No, I'm not driving anyone else's car until I drive my own." I had an accident in one of my teacher's cars. Wash the car and drive it over to another school. Drive it dry, you know?…

Now, Marlowe Morris is sitting between them. Marlow didn't know how to drive. He said, "Well, come on, Sid, you're going to learn how to drive tonight." So he gets Sid over. Now, we're right there by the UP station, the old train station there at 5th and Central. All right. Gets Sid on the wheel, Sid starts smiling, clutching the wheel like it's a gift to him, you know, someone has just given him something for Christmas. You know how he was. Oh, goody, goody.

Zoot So tells him where the ignition is, how to shift, clutch, out on clutch, out on the other one. Sid did this, started off, got up a little steam, and two blocks up we can see this signal changing. Red light pops up. Zoot says, "Put (laughs) on the brakes, Sid." Sid says, "Brakes?" I went under the seat. He had showed him everything. He kept telling him, "The other one, the other one." He didn't tell him the brake. He had reached over Marlow and grabbed the steering wheel, you know, and ended up in the gas…
